**Vietnam**,[[e]](#cite_note-16)[[f]](#cite_note-17) officially the **Socialist Republic of Viet Nam** (**SRV**),[[g]](#cite_note-18)[[h]](#cite_note-19) is a country at the eastern edge of [Mainland Southeast Asia](/wiki/Mainland_Southeast_Asia "Mainland Southeast Asia"). With an area of about 331,000 square kilometres and a population of over 102 million, it is the world's [16th-most populous country](/wiki/List_of_countries_and_dependencies_by_population "List of countries and dependencies by population"). One of two [communist states](/wiki/Communist_state "Communist state") in [Southeast Asia](/wiki/Southeast_Asia "Southeast Asia"),[[i]](#cite_note-20) Vietnam is bordered by [China](/wiki/China "China") to the north, and [Laos](/wiki/Laos "Laos") and [Cambodia](/wiki/Cambodia "Cambodia") to the west; it lies along the [Gulf of Thailand](/wiki/Gulf_of_Thailand "Gulf of Thailand") to the southwest and the [South China Sea](/wiki/South_China_Sea "South China Sea") to the east, where it has shared and [disputed maritime borders](/wiki/Territorial_disputes_in_the_South_China_Sea "Territorial disputes in the South China Sea") with other countries. Its capital is [Hanoi](/wiki/Hanoi "Hanoi"), while its [largest city](/wiki/List_of_cities_in_Vietnam#Largest_cities_by_population "List of cities in Vietnam") is [Ho Chi Minh City](/wiki/Ho_Chi_Minh_City "Ho Chi Minh City").

Vietnam was inhabited by the [Paleolithic](/wiki/Paleolithic "Paleolithic") age, with states established in the first millennium BC on the [Red River Delta](/wiki/Red_River_Delta "Red River Delta") in modern-day [northern Vietnam](/wiki/Northern_Vietnam "Northern Vietnam").[[12]](#cite_note-21) The [Han dynasty](/wiki/Han_dynasty "Han dynasty") annexed northern and central Vietnam, which were subsequently under [Chinese rule](/wiki/Vietnam_under_Chinese_rule "Vietnam under Chinese rule") from 111 BC until the [first dynasty](/wiki/Ng%C3%B4_dynasty "Ngô dynasty") emerge

The [1890 United States census](/wiki/1890_United_States_census "1890 United States census") showed a total population of 1,515,301, the foreign-born were 639,943 at 42%. The city did not trust the accuracy of the census so conducted an 1890 New York City Police census. This census revealed a population of 1,710,715.[[8]](#cite_note-8)
During the early 20th century, from 1900 to 1940, New York City's population was predominantly White, accounting for over 93% of the population, with the Black community constituting less than 3%. By the 1950s, the White population decreased to around 90%, while the Black population increased to nearly 10%. From 1970 to 1980, more pronounced shifts occurred, with the White population dropping to 60.72%, the Black population increasing to 25.23%, and a notable rise in the Hispanic/Latino population to 19.88%. The 1990s brought further diversification, with the White population falling to 44.66% by 2000, and growth in the Black, Asian, and Hispanic/Latino populations. The most recent decade from 2010 to 2020 saw a continued decrease in the White population to 34.09%, significant growth in the Asian population to 15.73%, stability in the Black population around 22-25%, and growth in the Hispanic/Latino community to 28.29%. The Other or Mixed category also grew to 28.11%. Throughout this period, New York City remained a hub for immigrants, with the foreign-born population peaking at 37.51% in 2010. Overall, these trends reflect the transformation of New York City into an increasingly multicultural metropolis, with a progressive decline in the White population and expanding representation of Black, Asian, Hispanic/Latino, and Other or Mixed groups.[[1]](#cite_note-nycrace-1)[[9]](#cite_note-9)

A sign-language [trade](/wiki/Trade "Trade") [pidgin](/wiki/Pidgin "Pidgin"), known as [Plains Indian Sign Language](/wiki/Plains_Indian_Sign_Language "Plains Indian Sign Language"), Plains Standard or Plains Sign Talk, arose among the [Native Americans of the plains](/wiki/Plains_Indians "Plains Indians"). Each signing nation had a separate signed version of their oral language, that was used by the hearing, and these were not mutually intelligible. Plains Standard was used to communicate between these nations. It seems to have started in Texas and then spread north, through the [Great Plains](/wiki/Great_Plains "Great Plains"), as far as [British Columbia](/wiki/British_Columbia "British Columbia"). There are still a few users today, especially among the [Crow](/wiki/Crow_Indians "Crow Indians"), [Cheyenne](/wiki/Cheyenne_Indians "Cheyenne Indians"), and [Arapaho](/wiki/Arapaho "Arapaho"). Unlike other sign languages developed by hearing people, it shares the spatial grammar of deaf sign languages. Through intergenerational transmission, Plains Sign Talk became a working language still in use today in some Deaf First Nations or Native American communities.

As Plains Sign Talk was so widespread and was a spectrum of dialects and accents, it probably hosted several languages under its umbrella. One is potentially Navajo Sign Language which is in use by a sole Navajo clan.

Additionally, [Plateau Sign Language](/wiki/Plateau_Sign_Language "Plateau Sign Language") existed alongside Plains Sign Talk as either a trade pidgin or another language around the [Columbia Plateau](/wiki/Columbia_Plateau "Columbia Plateau") and surrounding regions.
